theme: Search/SEO and referral data: Bing/Google keyword volume tools, SERP scrapers, Common Crawl web graph, backlink datasets, AI-bot crawler traffic stats (Cloudflare, Vercel)

candidates.name: cc-webgraph
candidates.what_it_holds: Java/shell tooling (WebGraph framework integration) to build host- and domain-level web graphs and compute PageRank/Harmonic Centrality from Common Crawl. No data committed in-repo; actual vertex/edge files and ranking outputs are announced separately on commoncrawl.org (large, S3-hosted).
candidates.why_useful: Could be re-run to derive a longitudinal 'web-graph rank' for airbnb.com vs vrbo.com/booking.com/expedia.com as an engagement/authority proxy (gap 5, 19). We already hold a CDX index over airbnb.com; this is the tool that turns crawl data into rank numbers.
candidates.size_hint: tooling only; underlying graphs are multi-GB, off-repo
candidates.last_activity: actively referenced, exact date not shown
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: extends our existing airbnb.com CDX index (2.08M rows) rather than duplicating it

candidates.name: cc-crawl-statistics
candidates.what_it_holds: Python pipeline that counts/aggregates per-crawl statistics from Common Crawl URL indexes: unique URLs, unique hosts/domains/TLDs, MIME types, protocol (HTTP/HTTPS), languages, per monthly crawl from ~2008-09 through at least 2022-05 (ongoing). No CSV/Parquet committed; pulls from s3://commoncrawl/crawl-analysis/.
candidates.why_useful: Could give a crude 'share of web indexed' time series by host, potentially proxying travel-site web presence/engagement trend over years, complementing our existing CDX/WARC captures.
candidates.size_hint: code only; pre-computed stats on S3 are modest CSVs per crawl

candidates.name: cdx-toolkit
candidates.what_it_holds: Python client that queries CDX indexes across both Common Crawl and the Internet Archive Wayback Machine with one API, iterating captures for a given domain/URL pattern and fetching WARC records. (Fetch to this exact URL 404'd on this pass; repo is well-known/widely cited — verify existence before relying on it.)
candidates.why_useful: Would generalize our existing airbnb.com CDX/WARC pull (2.08M rows, 3,000 renders) to competitor domains (vrbo.com, booking.com's alternative-accommodation pages, expedia.com) for a comparable point-in-time web-presence panel.

candidates.name: gau (getallurls)
candidates.what_it_holds: CLI (Go, MIT, 5.1k stars, 171 commits) that fetches all known URLs for a domain from Wayback Machine, Common Crawl, and AlienVault OTX in one pass; supports date-range and MIME filters, JSON output.
candidates.why_useful: One-command way to enumerate historical URL sets for competitor STR/OTA sites (Vrbo, Booking alt-accommodation, Sonder, Vacasa) across archives, e.g. to count listing/market pages seen over time as a rough supply/presence proxy (gap 9).
candidates.time_coverage: as far back as Wayback/CC coverage goes per domain
candidates.size_hint: tooling only; output size depends on domain

candidates.name: waybackpy
candidates.what_it_holds: Python package/CLI (MIT, 604 stars, 497 commits) wrapping Wayback Machine's CDX Server API, Availability API, and Save API — search archived snapshots near a given date, list oldest/newest captures.
candidates.why_useful: Point-in-time retrieval of archived airbnb.com and competitor pages (pricing pages, city landing pages, IR pages) by exact date — useful for vintage/point-in-time captures (gap 4/17) beyond our current Common Crawl-only WARC renders.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: complements our existing Common Crawl WARC renders (3,000) with Wayback-specific point-in-time capture

candidates.name: gtab (Google Trends Anchor Bank)
candidates.what_it_holds: Python library (MIT, 217 commits, 123 stars, CIKM 2020 paper implementation) that calibrates Google Trends against a bank of anchor queries so multiple search terms become comparable on an absolute 0-100+ scale rather than Trends' relative/rounded 5-term-max output; anchor lists and example configs committed (e.g. anchor_candidate_list.txt).
candidates.why_useful: Directly the 'gtab / anchored Google Trends' method flagged as a target in gap 17. Our own Google Trends work (9 terms, not point-in-time) failed as pulled; gtab is the standard fix for making Trends pulls calibrated and comparable across refresh dates — worth testing as a longer-run, comparable alternative before writing off Trends entirely.
candidates.time_coverage: as far back as Google Trends allows (2004-present) once an anchor bank is built for the window
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: we already hold raw Google Trends pulls (9 terms, not point-in-time); this is the calibration method, not a duplicate dataset

candidates.name: ai.robots.txt
candidates.what_it_holds: Curated, machine-generated list (robots.json source, MIT, 746 commits) of known AI-crawler user agents (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, etc.) exported as robots.txt/.htaccess/nginx/Caddy/HAProxy/lighttpd block-lists plus a table-of-bot-metrics.md; links out to a 'Bot Ledger' directory and an 'AI Crawler Census' that tracks allow/block status across top sites. No traffic-volume numbers in this repo itself.
candidates.why_useful: Reference list of AI-bot identifiers needed to build any AI-referral-traffic measurement (gap 19); the linked 'AI Crawler Census' (tracks which top sites block which AI bots) is a candidate to check separately for site-level allow/block time series, though not fetchable this pass (404 on darkvisitors/agents).
candidates.time_coverage: current snapshot only (list of active bots, not a volume time series)

candidates.name: AgentECHO
candidates.what_it_holds: Self-hosted analytics platform (Go/TypeScript/Next.js/ClickHouse) to detect, classify, and monetize AI bot traffic (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, etc.) on a site the operator controls; ships code only, no third-party dataset — it produces data only from traffic it observes on a deployed site.
candidates.why_useful: Illustrates current tooling for AI-crawler traffic measurement (gap 19) but has no usable pre-existing dataset for ABNB or travel; would only be useful if deployed on a site we control.

candidates.name: python-mwviews
candidates.what_it_holds: Python library (MIT, 38 commits) to query Wikimedia pageview statistics from both static dumps and the live API: per-article, per-project view counts, top-articles-by-country, daily/monthly granularity, parallelized requests.
candidates.why_useful: One-command pull of Airbnb's (and Vrbo/Booking/Expedia/Vacasa's) Wikipedia pageview history as a free, long-run public-attention proxy (gap 5: engagement/web-traffic estimates) — Wikipedia pageviews are public back to ~2007-2015 depending on project, and this tool is simpler than hitting the raw REST API directly.
candidates.time_coverage: Wikimedia pageview API coverage, ~2015-present (hourly dumps back to 2007 for some projects)
candidates.size_hint: tooling only; per-article series are tiny

candidates.name: CrUX (Chrome UX Report community repo)
candidates.what_it_holds: Community repo (Apache-2.0, 79 commits) of SQL/BigQuery queries, JS API-call samples, AppScript and Colab notebooks for querying the Chrome UX Report public dataset (real-user experience/traffic-adjacent metrics per origin, hosted in BigQuery, not in this repo).
candidates.why_useful: CrUX's public BigQuery dataset covers per-origin real-Chrome-user metrics for airbnb.com and competitor domains monthly since 2017; this repo is just the query cookbook needed to pull it (gap 5 popularity-rank angle), not itself a data cache.
candidates.size_hint: queries only; underlying BigQuery public dataset is large

candidates.name: app-store-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Node.js module (MIT, 1.4k stars, 164 commits) scraping Apple App Store metadata: app details, search results, ratings/reviews, version history, developer pages, category rankings ('collections').
candidates.why_useful: Could be run periodically going forward to build an Airbnb-app category-ranking / rating-count time series as a downloads/engagement proxy (gap 5); does not backfill history (no historical dataset committed), only forward point-in-time snapshots.
candidates.time_coverage: point-in-time only from whenever run; no historical archive
candidates.last_activity: 164 commits; author notes low active maintenance, PR-review-only

candidates.name: google-play-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Node.js module (MIT, 3k+ stars, 496 commits) scraping Google Play: app details, curated collections/rankings, reviews (paginated/bulk), developer app lists, permissions/data-safety info.
candidates.why_useful: Same use case as app-store-scraper but for Android/Google Play — Airbnb app ranking and review-volume snapshots as an engagement proxy (gap 5); again forward-only, no historical archive, and author states it's no longer actively maintained beyond community PRs.

candidates.name: Majestic Million (top 1M domains by referring subnets)
candidates.what_it_holds: Freely downloadable CSV (~80MB, CC BY 3.0 licensed) of the top 1 million root domains ranked by referring subnets/IPs, regenerated daily from Majestic's own crawl/link index; columns include GlobalRank, TLD, RefSubNets, RefIPs, rank deltas. Hosted at majestic.com/reports/majestic-million, not on GitHub itself, though community GitHub mirrors of historical snapshots exist sporadically (not verified this pass).
candidates.why_useful: A free, dated, backlink-based domain-authority ranking that could track airbnb.com vs vrbo.com/booking.com/expedia.com over time if snapshots are saved daily going forward (gap 19 adjacent: backlink/authority as an engagement proxy). No historical archive by default — would need our own daily pull starting now.
candidates.time_coverage: daily snapshot only (no historical archive without self-collection)

notes: Hard blocker: this session's WebSearch tool returned 'budget exhausted (200 of 200)' on the very first query, before I personally had used any — the 200-call cap is evidently shared across all concurrent scout subagents in this sweep, not per-agent. All 4 WebSearch queries failed immediately, so this modality was executed almost entirely via WebFetch on individually guessed/known GitHub URLs and github.com/topics/<tag> listing pages instead of true web search or gh search (which was off-limits anyway). github.com/search?q=... also started 429-rate-limiting after 3 calls (Retry-After: 3600s), so broad keyword search on GitHub itself was unavailable for most of the run; topics pages worked as a partial substitute. Net effect: coverage here is narrower and more reliant on prior knowledge of specific repo names than other scouts likely achieved with a working WebSearch budget. Recommend a re-run of this theme once the WebSearch budget resets, focused specifically on: (1) a genuine Cloudflare Radar API/dataset client (none confirmed this pass), (2) Vercel bot-traffic reports/datasets (not reached at all), (3) any GitHub mirror of Common Crawl's actual host/domain-rank output files (only tooling found, not the computed rankings), (4) the 'AI Crawler Census' and 'Bot Ledger' properties referenced by ai.robots.txt, which could hold real per-site AI-bot allow/block time series relevant to gap 19 but were not independently reachable (darkvisitors/agents 404'd). Most 'keyword research'/'backlink'/'SERP scraper' GitHub topics are dominated by SaaS-wrapper or paid-API-key tools with zero committed data — low yield for this theme generally; the real value in this theme turned out to be Common-Crawl/Wayback *tooling* (gau, waybackpy, cdx-toolkit-class tools, gtab) that could extend our EXISTING airbnb.com CDX/WARC captures to competitor domains, rather than any new committed dataset.
